title: Master crash before the observer's enable loses it: the map has advanced, nothing retries, and flush fails at L163 on a table left DISABLED
cause: QuotaObserverChore.updateTableQuota writes the observance row and advances its in-memory snapshot before its single enable attempt, and the pending enable is not recorded anywhere that survives a failure.
trigger: The active master is killed after the observer's put and map update, or before a run whose connection already knows hbase:quota. The enable fails, the next run is a no-op, and the next master initializes with the table still DISABLED.
consequence: admin.flush fails with TableNotEnabledException thrown at AbstractStateMachineTableProcedure.java:163, and the table stays DISABLED until an operator acts.
premises: The observer's single enable attempt fails because no master is running; in the workload it has client retries = 0.
In the workload the observer's map outlives the crash because it lives in the test JVM; the same no-retry follows from any failed enable.
A master kill is in the fault model; the reproduction injects only SingleProcessHBaseCluster.killMaster and restarts the master on its old port.
The E-stored-but-never-locked branch was not reached on the real system; the confirmation rests on the E-never-stored branch.
